title: The Birth of Jesus and the Magi
summary: Mary is found with child before she and Joseph come together, and Joseph, a just man, plans to divorce her quietly until an angel tells him in a dream that the child is of the Holy Ghost and is to be named Jesus. Wise men from the east come to Jerusalem asking where the king of the Jews is born. Herod learns from the chief priests that the Christ is to be born in Bethlehem. The star leads the wise men to the house, where they worship the child and offer gold, frankincense and myrrh.

title: Flight to Egypt and Return to Nazareth
summary: An angel warns Joseph in a dream to take the child and Mary to Egypt because Herod will seek to kill him, and they leave by night. Herod, furious that the wise men have not returned, has all boys in Bethlehem aged two and under killed, which Matthew connects to Jeremiah's words about Rachel weeping. After Herod dies, an angel tells Joseph to return, and warned again, he settles in Nazareth, which Matthew says fulfills the words 'He shall be called a Nazarene.'

title: The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus
summary: John the Baptist preaches repentance in the wilderness of Judaea, wearing camel's hair and eating locusts and wild honey, and baptizes crowds in the Jordan. Jesus comes from Galilee to be baptized; John objects, but Jesus says it fulfills righteousness. As he comes up, the heavens open, the Spirit descends like a dove, and a voice says, 'This is my beloved Son.' Led by the Spirit into the wilderness, Jesus fasts forty days and answers the devil's three temptations with scripture.

title: Calling the First Disciples
summary: After John is imprisoned, Jesus withdraws to Galilee and settles in Capernaum, which Matthew says fulfills Isaiah's words about a great light for Zebulun and Naphtali. He begins preaching, 'Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.' By the Sea of Galilee he calls the fishermen Simon Peter and Andrew, and then James and John, who leave their nets to follow him. Jesus goes through Galilee teaching and healing, and crowds from Syria, Decapolis, Jerusalem and Judaea follow him.

title: The Sermon on the Mount
summary: Seeing the crowds, Jesus goes up a mountain and teaches his disciples. He opens with the Beatitudes, calls them salt and light, and says he has come to fulfill the law, then reinterprets commands on anger, adultery, oaths, retaliation and love of enemies. He teaches how to give, pray and fast, and warns against treasure on earth, anxiety and judging, ending with the two gates and the house on the rock. The crowds are astonished that he teaches with authority.

title: Healings and Calming the Storm
summary: Jesus heals a leper, a centurion's servant, Peter's mother-in-law and a paralytic. He calms a storm and sends demons into a herd of pigs, and calls Matthew the tax collector. On the way to a ruler's house he heals a woman who touched his cloak, then raises the ruler's daughter. He tells his disciples to pray for laborers for the harvest.

title: Sending Out the Twelve
summary: Jesus gives his twelve disciples authority over unclean spirits and diseases and names them, from Simon Peter to Judas Iscariot, who betrayed him. He sends them to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, telling them to preach that the kingdom of heaven is at hand, to heal, and to take no money or extra clothes. He warns of arrests, floggings and family division, tells them not to fear those who kill the body, and says whoever receives them receives him.

title: Jesus and John the Baptist
summary: John the Baptist, in prison, sends disciples to ask whether Jesus is the one who is to come. Jesus tells them to report what they hear and see: the blind see, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor have good news preached. He tells the crowds that John is more than a prophet, rebukes the cities that did not repent, and thanks the Father, then invites the weary to take his yoke.

title: Sabbath Controversies and the Sign of Jonah
summary: The Pharisees object when Jesus' disciples pluck grain on the Sabbath; he cites David eating the showbread and says the Son of man is lord of the Sabbath, and he heals a man's withered hand in the synagogue. The Pharisees plot to destroy him. When he casts out a demon, they say he does it by Beelzebub. Asked for a sign, he points to the sign of the prophet Jonas, and he says whoever does the Father's will is his brother, sister and mother.

title: Parables of the Kingdom
summary: Jesus sits by the sea and teaches a crowd in parables, beginning with the sower and the four soils, and says he speaks in parables so that those who see do not see. He explains the sower to his disciples, then tells the parables of the wheat and tares, the mustard seed, the leaven, the hidden treasure, the pearl and the net. When he returns to his hometown, people are offended, and he does not do many mighty works there because of their unbelief.

title: Feeding the Five Thousand and Walking on Water
summary: Herod the tetrarch, hearing of Jesus, says John the Baptist has risen; Matthew recounts that Herod, bound by an oath after Herodias's daughter danced at his birthday, had John beheaded. Jesus withdraws, but crowds follow, and he heals the sick and feeds about five thousand men with five loaves and two fish, with twelve baskets left. That night he comes to the disciples walking on the sea. Peter walks toward him, begins to sink, and is saved.

title: Peter's Confession and the Transfiguration
summary: At Caesarea Philippi Jesus asks who people say the Son of man is, and Peter says, 'Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.' Jesus says he will build his church on this rock and gives Peter the keys of the kingdom. He then foretells his suffering, death and resurrection. Six days later he is transfigured on a mountain before Peter, James and John, with Moses and Elias, and a voice from a cloud says, 'This is my beloved Son.' He then heals a boy.

title: Teaching on Forgiveness and Greatness
summary: The disciples ask who is greatest in the kingdom, and Jesus sets a child among them and says they must become like children. He warns against causing little ones to stumble, tells the parable of the lost sheep, and gives steps for confronting a brother who sins. When Peter asks if he should forgive seven times, Jesus answers seventy times seven and tells the parable of the unforgiving servant, forgiven a huge debt but refusing to forgive a small one.

title: The Rich Young Man
summary: Crossing into Judaea, Jesus answers the Pharisees on divorce, blesses little children, and meets a rich young man who asks what good thing he must do for eternal life; told to sell what he has and follow him, he goes away sorrowful. Jesus says it is hard for the rich to enter the kingdom and promises reward to those who left everything. He tells of the laborers in the vineyard, foretells his death a third time, and heals two blind men near Jericho.

title: The Triumphal Entry and Temple Cleansing
summary: Jesus enters Jerusalem on a donkey and colt as crowds spread cloaks and branches and cry 'Hosanna to the son of David.' He drives the sellers and money changers from the temple, quoting 'My house shall be called the house of prayer', and heals the blind and lame there. On the way back he curses a fig tree, which withers. Challenged by the chief priests on his authority, he asks about John's baptism and tells the parables of the two sons and the wicked husbandmen.

title: Teaching in the Temple and the Olivet Discourse
summary: In the temple Jesus tells the parable of the wedding feast and answers questions about paying tribute to Caesar, the resurrection, and the greatest commandment. He denounces the scribes and Pharisees with a series of woes and laments over Jerusalem. On the Mount of Olives he foretells the temple's destruction, wars and persecution, and the coming of the Son of man, and tells the parables of the ten virgins and the talents, ending with the judgment of the sheep and goats.

title: The Last Supper and Gethsemane
summary: The chief priests plot to arrest Jesus, and a woman anoints his head with expensive ointment at Bethany; the disciples object, and Jesus says she has prepared him for burial. Judas agrees to betray him for thirty pieces of silver. At the Passover meal Jesus says one of the twelve will betray him, gives the bread and cup, and foretells that Peter will deny him. In Gethsemane he prays three times, and Judas arrives with an armed crowd and kisses him.

title: Trial, Crucifixion and Burial
summary: Jesus is taken to Caiaphas, where false witnesses speak, and the high priest accuses him of blasphemy. Peter denies him three times and weeps. Judas returns the silver and hangs himself. Before Pilate, Jesus says little; the crowd chooses Barabbas, Pilate washes his hands, and Jesus is scourged, mocked, and crucified at Golgotha between two robbers. At his death the temple veil tears and the earth shakes. Joseph of Arimathaea buries him, and guards are set at the tomb.

title: The Resurrection and the Great Commission
summary: At dawn on the first day of the week Mary Magdalene and the other Mary come to the tomb, where an earthquake and an angel roll back the stone; the angel says Jesus has risen and tells them to tell the disciples to go to Galilee. On the way Jesus meets them, and they worship him. The guards are paid by the chief priests to say the disciples stole the body. On a mountain in Galilee Jesus meets the eleven, some of whom doubt, and sends them to make disciples of all nations.
